samples.summary: The new read-path clamp in `resolvePageSetup` is bypassed by both exporters, contrary to the invariant the diff documents
samples.evidence: `packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:797` (new docstring) asserts "the editor, the ruler, `MemDocStore`, `YorkieDocStore`, the CLI's pagination and PDF export all reach the page setup through it" — i.e. `resolvePageSetup` is "the single read path". It is not. `packages/docs/src/export/pdf-exporter.ts:87` reads `const setup = doc.pageSetup ?? DEFAULT_PAGE_SETUP;` and feeds it straight to `getEffectiveDimensions`/`computeLayout`/`paginateLayout` (lines 88-92) with no clamp; `packages/docs/src/export/docx-exporter.ts:162` likewise passes `doc.pageSetup ?? DEFAULT_PAGE_SETUP` into `buildSectPrXml`. Both are reached from the frontend with the raw CRDT document (`packages/frontend/src/app/docs/pdf-actions.ts:30`, `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docx-actions.ts:50`, both called with `editor.getStore().getDocument()` from the export menu). So the exact geometry the change exists to neutralise — a collaborator's hostile/corrupt `root.pageSetup` with NaN, negative, or page-swallowing margins — still reaches `paginateLayout` (contentHeight <= 0, `packages/docs/src/view/pagination.ts:55`) and the DOCX `<w:sectPr>` writer, producing a broken/oversized export or a pagination pass with a non-positive content box. Fix belongs on the two exporters (wrap in `resolvePageSetup`), or the new docstring's claim must be narrowed.

samples.summary: `DocStore.setPageSetup` is a public write path that does not pass through the new `assertUsablePageSetup` guard
samples.evidence: The new guard lives in `initialize()` (`packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:2058-2070`), but `setPageSetup` is part of the exported `DocStore` interface (`packages/docs/src/store/store.ts:28`) and is implemented at `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:2710` and `packages/docs/src/store/memory.ts:98`. Anything holding a store (the frontend holds one in `storeRef`, `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-view.tsx:325`) can write unusable geometry into the CRDT without the RangeError check. Today only the editor calls it, so this is a latent bypass rather than a live one; the read-path clamp partially covers it, except at the two exporter sites noted separately.

samples.summary: The new line-separator fold in the Markdown serializer rests on an invariant the paste path violates: runs legitimately carry `\n`
samples.evidence:
`packages/docs/src/serialize/markdown.ts:347` states "A run's `text` is inline content — the model puts a paragraph break in a new block, never inside a run — so a line break in one is either import noise or an injection." HTML paste disagrees: `packages/docs/src/view/clipboard.ts:689` pushes `{ text: '\n', style }` for every `
`, a legitimate soft line break in the model (and `serializeText` still emits it verbatim). After this change every such break is silently folded to a space in Markdown export only, so `.md` and `.txt` exports of the same document now disagree on line structure. Not a crash — but the stated invariant is false, and the producer at clipboard.ts:689 was not considered.

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo. `resolvePageSetup` (packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:810-841) is a clamping read path whose docstring (types.ts:793-809) asserts it is "the single read path ... and it is the only place that sees geometry we did not validate ourselves", naming the collaborator CRDT write as the threat. Both exporters bypass it: pdf-exporter.ts:87 does `const setup = doc.pageSetup ?? DEFAULT_PAGE_SETUP` and feeds it unclamped to getEffectiveDimensions/computeLayout/paginateLayout (lines 88-92); docx-exporter.ts:162 passes `doc.pageSetup ?? DEFAULT_PAGE_SETUP` into buildSectPrXml. A repo-wide grep shows no `resolvePageSetup` reference anywhere under packages/docs/src/export/. The bypass is reachable with unvalidated data: docs-export-button.tsx:53 invokes the export actions with `editor.getStore().getDocument()`, and YorkieDocStore.getDocument (yorkie-doc-store.ts:604-606) attaches `readPageSetup(root.pageSetup)` raw — unlike getPageSetup() at :661-666 which does clamp — so a hostile/corrupt remote pageSetup flows into paginateLayout, where contentHeight has no floor (pagination.ts:55), and into the DOCX sectPr writer. Blast-radius lane: a new guard with a reachable bypass / an asserted invariant violated at sites outside the diff. No refutation ground applies.

finding.summary: DOCX import writes an unvalidated `pageSetup` straight into the CRDT, bypassing the new `assertUsablePageSetup` invariant
finding.evidence: The diff states the invariant on `writePageSetup` (`packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:2062`) because a closed/NaN content box "is written into the CRDT for every collaborator". But `writePageSetup` is not the only page-setup writer. `DocxImporter.import()` produces `{ blocks, pageSetup }` (`packages/docs/src/import/docx-importer.ts:158`) where `parsePageSetup` (`packages/docs/src/import/docx-parser.ts:288-319`) computes `width = Math.round(twipsToPx(parseInt(w,10)))` with no finiteness or positivity check (a non-numeric `w:w` yields NaN) and copies `w:pgMar` top/bottom/left/right verbatim — negative margins and margins summing past the page are all accepted. That document is then committed by `store.setDocument(pending)` at `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-view.tsx:356`, which never reaches `assertUsablePageSetup`. The result is exactly the state the new guard exists to prevent: a page box `paginateLayout`, the ruler and the PDF exporter cannot consume, persisted for every collaborator. Fix belongs on the import/`setDocument` path (or in `resolvePageSetup`), not on the new guard.

verdict.reason: The unvalidated import writer described in the finding is not present in this tree. `sectPrLengthPx` (packages/docs/src/import/docx-parser.ts:302-314) rejects non-finite page/margin lengths, rejects non-positive page dimensions and negative margins, and falls back to defaults — so a non-numeric `w:w` cannot yield NaN. `parsePageSetup` does not copy `w:pgMar` verbatim: it returns `resolvePageSetup({paperSize, orientation, margins})` (docx-parser.ts:347), and `resolvePageSetup` (packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:810-841) applies `usableSize` (types.ts:759-763), `usableMargin` (types.ts:766-770) and `fitMargins` (types.ts:777-791), which proportionally shrinks any margin pair that would leave less than MIN_CONTENT_PX against the orientation-effective box. That is precisely the predicate `assertUsablePageSetup` (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:962-993) enforces, so the value handed to `store.setDocument(pending)` (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-view.tsx:356) already satisfies the invariant. The read path clamps again as well (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:661-666, packages/docs/src/store/memory.ts:95, packages/cli/src/docs/paginate.ts:26). The reviewer's own proposed fix location (`resolvePageSetup` / the import path) is already implemented.

finding.summary: The new markdown URL gate silently drops legitimate relative image sources and relative/anchor hrefs produced elsewhere in the app, in every consumer of `serializeMarkdown`
finding.evidence: `isSafeUrl` only accepts absolute http/https/mailto/tel (`packages/core/src/url/index.ts:24`), so `isSafeImageSrc` / `isEmittableUrl` now reject anything relative. Out-of-diff producers emit exactly that: `resolveImageUrl()` (`packages/frontend/src/app/docs/export-utils.ts:12-18`) returns a bare `/images/<id>` whenever `VITE_BACKEND_API_URL` is unset (same-origin deployment) and that value is stored as the image `src` by `docsImageUploader` → `insertImageFromFile` (`image-insert.ts:61-68`); HTML paste stores raw `<a href>` attributes verbatim, including `#anchor` and `/relative` targets (`packages/docs/src/view/clipboard.ts:597-599`, `:699-701`). Those images now serialize as the `[image]` placeholder and those links lose their destination in every Markdown output — the new frontend Export menu, the CLI's `docs content --format md` (`packages/cli/src/docs/content.ts:129`) and, because it shares the docs serializer, `slides content --format md` (`packages/cli/src/slides/content.ts:184`). Silent lossy behaviour change on content the gate was not aimed at.

verdict.reason: The finding asserts that the new markdown URL gate routes everything through `isSafeUrl` and therefore drops relative image sources and relative/anchor hrefs. The code does not do this. `isEmittableUrl` (packages/docs/src/serialize/markdown.ts:295-300) only calls `isSafeUrl` when `HAS_SCHEME` (markdown.ts:271) matches; a reference with no scheme is accepted outright unless it is scheme-relative (`//`, `\\`, `/\` — markdown.ts:280). So `/images/<id>` produced by resolveImageUrl (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/export-utils.ts:12-18) when VITE_BACKEND_API_URL is unset, plus `#anchor`, `./a.png`, `../a.png`, `a.png`, `?page=2`, all pass. `isSafeImageSrc` (markdown.ts:313-319) delegates to the same predicate, so images behave identically. This is not incidental: the doc comment at markdown.ts:286-293 names exactly this case, and tests at packages/docs/test/serialize/markdown.test.ts:594-612 assert `[click me](/uploads/a.png)`, `(./a.png)`, `(../a.png)`, `(a.png)`, `(sub/dir/a.png)`, `(#section-2)`, `(?page=2)` and `![pic](/uploads/a.png)`, `![pic](./a.png)`, `![pic](#anchor)` are preserved. There is a single `serializeMarkdown` implementation (markdown.ts:38, exported at src/index.ts:191 and src/node.ts:165), so the claimed downstream breakage in packages/cli/src/docs/content.ts:129, packages/cli/src/slides/content.ts:184 and packages/frontend/src/app/docs/text-actions.ts:44 does not occur — they all inherit the relative-permissive gate. The described lossy behaviour is not present in the repository.
